video_title: Glen "Big Baby" Davis: How I Survived Federal Prison

quotes.speaker: Glen "Big Baby" Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis on how a chance encounter led to his acting career
quotes.excerpt: I'm doing a set on stage and some woman walks up to me and she's like, 'Do you want to act?'
quotes.quote: I started being a comedian first. I'm doing a set on stage and some woman walks up to me and she's like, 'Do you want to act?' I'm like, 'Yeah, sure, why not?' I get my first gig for Shameless. I started booking these gigs, then I did Lincoln Lawyer, then I started doing some small films, some indie films. The next thing you know, I'm in New York and 50 Cent is performing. As he's performing, he's like, 'Yo, Big Baby, what's up?' I'm like, 'Yo, what's up, 50?'

quotes.speaker: Glen "Big Baby" Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis on his difficult upbringing in Baton Rouge
quotes.excerpt: I grew up in a very special place. Growing up in a drug-infested neighborhood, killings every day.
quotes.quote: I grew up in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. I would have to say my upbringing was pretty tough. Growing up in a drug-infested neighborhood, killings every day. Mom on drugs, didn't know who my father was at the time. I grew up in a very special place.

quotes.speaker: Glen "Big Baby" Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis on the origin of his 'Big Baby' nickname
quotes.excerpt: I got the name in the hood. I was a big kid and I had a baby face.
quotes.quote: I got the name in the hood. That's how I got the name Big Baby. I was a big kid and I had a baby face. Everybody was like, 'That's Big Baby, look at Big Baby.'

quotes.speaker: Glen "Big Baby" Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis on his draft experience and winning a championship
quotes.excerpt: I got drafted to the Seattle SuperSonics and traded to the Boston Celtics for Ray Allen.
quotes.quote: I got drafted to the Seattle SuperSonics and traded to the Boston Celtics for Ray Allen. Then, I won a championship with the Boston Celtics and a new door opened up. Being a Boston Celtic and winning a championship was super cool.

quotes.speaker: Glen "Big Baby" Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis on the intensity of the Celtics-Lakers rivalry
quotes.excerpt: Lakers and Celtics and that rivalry is epic. Bill Russell, Jerry West, those guys set the stage.
quotes.quote: Lakers and Celtics and that rivalry is epic. Magic, Larry Bird, Kevin McHale, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, those guys set the stage. Bill Russell, Jerry West, those guys set the stage for that rivalry, and now to be able to be a part of another rivalry, Celtics and Lakers, is epic.

quotes.speaker: Glen "Big Baby" Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis on the dangers of bringing friends into professional sports

With that being said, it's the fact that I didn't know what truly was going on when they came to me. I didn't know how to do it. I just knew like, 'All right, cool, we got this money.'

quotes.speaker: Glen "Big Baby" Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis on his legal defense and the insurance fraud case
quotes.excerpt: I called the healthcare place and I was like, 'Hey, I got nothing to do with this.'
quotes.quote: I called the healthcare place and I was like, 'Hey, I got nothing to do with this.' I have no idea what was going on. I have a real injury here. I'm trying to get real money back from what I've done. I'm dealing with my financial advisor and my business manager, the guy who runs my whole life, signing papers that he shouldn't have signed, and I'm me believing in him. So, I called my financial advisor, Edgar Abrams, and he's like, 'Yeah, I can do this.' He said, 'Review it, sign it, send it back.'

quotes.speaker: Glen "Big Baby" Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis on the scale of the NBA insurance fraud investigation
quotes.excerpt: Thousands of NBA players were investigated. They just let some of them go to jail.
quotes.quote: There was a lot of people that got investigated. Kendrick Perkins, you see him on ESPN, Tony Allen, he was literally the third person on the indictment, fourth person on the indictment with his wife. He's not walking in jail. Darius Miles, he's not walking in jail. And these guys got money, like thousands of dollars. Thousands of NBA players were investigated. They just let some of them go to jail. Some of them, the feds got, but then, right, like how Tony Allen, he didn't go to jail. He's still out.

quotes.speaker: Glen "Big Baby" Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis on the unfairness of his sentencing compared to others
quotes.excerpt: I won like half of them, but it doesn't matter, and the feds, they just have to win one.
quotes.quote: I won like half of them, but it doesn't matter, and the feds, they just have to win one. But they wouldn't give me a good plea deal. They wanted me to go to prison, and I was young. I was 19, 20 years old. They were just so aggressive. And then you look at all these guys that steal millions and get 24 months, 12 months, a year and a day. I'll never pay the money back.

quotes.speaker: Glen Davis

quotes.quote: Hell yeah, he knew exactly who I was. You could just tell. He wanted to ask me questions. He wanted to keep it cool, but he knew exactly who I was when I came up.

quotes.speaker: Glen Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis describes the poor conditions of Building 7

quotes.quote: Building 7 was the most horrible building. I'm talking about rusty nails, showers, rusty. In the shower thing is about this big, so I got to turn in sideways to shower. And then the beds, the beds were so small. I'm just like, I can't believe this. I got my little baby locker. I got my little locker and I'm just like, man, I need some toiletries, you know, I don't got shit. I didn't bring shit. All I did has money to put on my books and stuff like that, but I need to get some stuff.

quotes.speaker: Glen Davis
quotes.summary_phrase: Glen Davis on the lack of rehabilitation in prison
quotes.excerpt: I just really think, you know, they don't really truly understand what we truly have to go
quotes.quote: I just really think, you know, they don't really truly understand what we truly have to go to with reentry. You know what I mean? Like, sometimes halfway house is good for people. You know what I mean? Let them get their bearings before they go back into their own world and society to get better or just educational, right? Things that I was supposed to know at the halfway house that I I didn't know. Right? I thought I was going to go straight home, like, right? I'm I'm eligible for home confinement. Hey, let me go home. No, you're going to stay in this halfway house for as long as we think you should stay and then we're going to let you go. And then when we get the halfway house, we're going to treat you like you're in jail, right? Where you got to report every five seconds or whatever you got to do something. You can't do this, you can't do that. You got to do this, right? You know, I think the rehabilitation part is forgotten.
